Container.Name: chadash
Container.Overview:
Cha Dash is the front page of your home: one calm, live page that shows what is running across your homelab and what needs your attention. It reads from Unraid, Proxmox, Docker, Home Assistant, Frigate, Plex, Jellyfin, the *arr apps and more, about 26 services in all. It only reads: it never changes anything. Your credentials stay on this server, encrypted. There is no telemetry: Cha Dash talks only to the services you add.
This is a beta. Before the first start, give the appdata folder to the user the container runs as (uid 65532). In a terminal, run: mkdir -p /mnt/user/appdata/chadash; chown 65532:65532 /mnt/user/appdata/chadash; chmod 700 /mnt/user/appdata/chadash
Then start it and open the Web UI to create your account (the username starts as admin). The beta guide: https://github.com/ban-red/cha-dash/blob/main/docs/beta.md
Container.Changes: ### 0.2.0-beta.1 The first published beta: actions with plans, confirmations, undo and an audit log. What's in it: https://github.com/ban-red/cha-dash/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
Container.Requires: The appdata folder must belong to uid 65532 before the first start: mkdir -p /mnt/user/appdata/chadash; chown 65532:65532 /mnt/user/appdata/chadash; chmod 700 /mnt/user/appdata/chadash

Config.Name: Web UI port
Config.Description: The port you open Cha Dash on. The container always listens on 3696: change only this host side.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: The database and the key that unlocks the stored credentials. Back them up together. Owned by uid 65532 (see Requires).

Config.Name: Public URL
Config.Description: Optional. The https:// address you open Cha Dash at, such as https://dash.lab.example. Passkeys need it, and only work over HTTPS. Everything else works without it.

Config.Name: Trusted proxies
Config.Description: Optional. Behind a reverse proxy (SWAG, Nginx Proxy Manager, Traefik, Caddy): the proxy's IP address or subnet, comma-separated, such as 172.18.0.0/16. Cha Dash then believes the client address and HTTPS the proxy reports.
